sn1.44:1.1: The exact meaning of these items is open to interpretation. | _Āvaṭṭa_ here might be read as either “whirlpool” or “twist”.
sn1.44:1.2: _Patthara_ is probably a “spread” of grass, such as was laid down in rituals.
sn1.44:1.3: If the ocean is counted as the last item, the total is twelve. _Dvādasa_ can be an ordinal number. Thus I take the riddle as corresponding with the twelvefold “round” (_vaṭṭa_) of dependent origination. The “one root” is ignorance; the “two turnings” are name-and-form with consciousness; the “three stains” are ignorance, craving, and grasping; the “five spreads” are perhaps the five consequents starting with consciousness;
